messages:
OpsBot: :rotating_light: Incident alert: gpu-autoscale-queue-growth — HPA not reacting to custom metric 'inference_queue_depth' for inference-prod (region-us-west). Investigating.
Devon (oncall): I'm on it. seeing sustained queue growth on GPU pool A, token throttles and 429s in proxy logs.
Maya: saw spikes ~10:12 UTC, HPA shows stable desired=4, current=4, but queue depth > 120 for last 6m. HPA target is custom/queue-depth.
Samir: prometheus-adapter metrics look… sparse. `kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` returns empty list.
Devon (oncall): that explains HPA not scaling. is metrics-adapter behind? k8s-metrics-bot, any alerts from metrics pipeline?
k8s-metrics-bot: Alert: prometheus-scrape-errors high on prometheus-main (job=redwood-inference-exporter), last 5m error rate 78%. Adapter request latency spiked, 503s to adapter.
Maya: quick check — `kubectl logs -n monitoring deployment/prometheus-adapter` shows repeated `panic: unexpected EOF` and `timeout writing to remote read`.
Samir: looks like Prometheus remote_read/remote_write backlog causing adapter timeouts. I see TLS renegotiation errors on prometheus -> remote storage.
Devon (oncall): customer impact?
Customer Success: multiple customers reported increased latencies and occasional `model-unavailable` errors for large-payloads. No full-scale outages but severe degradation for heavy prompt workloads.
Maya: mitigation plan: 1) short-term scale down heavy-model routes to free GPU capacity; 2) fallback route to cpu-backed smaller model; 3) manual scale of HPA target nodes for immediate capacity; 4) restore metrics pipeline.
Samir: for metrics pipeline, I'm going to restart prometheus-adapter and rotate config for remote_write to reduce backlog. prepping for restart — will cordon nothing, just restart pod one at a time.
Devon (oncall): do manual GPU nodegroup scale now to relieve queue. Executing cloud CLI to increase nodepool-inference-prod by +3.
Maya: patching routing: set feature-flag `route:soft-fallback=true` for inference-prod in console to route new heavy requests to redwood-small. Doing now.
Devon (oncall): nodepool scale request sent; cloud response: scaling in progress (request id cl-0a1b2c). Expect nodes ready ~8-10m.
Samir: restarting prometheus-adapter pod now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter -n monitoring` — rolling restart in progress.
OpsBot: Deploy bot: rollout started for deployment/prometheus-adapter (monitoring).
Maya: switching a few high-volume customers to degraded mode (notify + reduce concurrency) — CS notified customers with temporary mitigation.
Customer Success: notified 3 affected customers at 10:19 UTC, offering priority support and status updates.
Samir: after restart, adapter logs show successful registration of custom metrics. `kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` now returns metrics for namespace inference-prod.
Devon (oncall): checking HPA now: `kubectl describe hpa inference-workers -n inference-prod` shows new metrics pulled and desired scaled to 7 (from 4). HPA triggered scale up.
Maya: routing changes reduced new heavy requests by ~40%, queue depth trending down from 130 -> 45 in 6m.
Devon (oncall): nodepool scaled; new nodes joined and pods scheduled. GPU throttling decreasing.
Samir: follow-up — we saw root cause: Prometheus remote storage TLS churn caused write timeouts; adapter requests were timing out and returning errors; HPA couldn't read custom metric so it stayed at lower replica count. Adding a circuit-breaker and backpressure metric on adapter.
Maya: oncall handoff — Devon, are you stable to continue? I'm taking next shift at 10:40 UTC.
Devon (oncall): handing to Maya. leaving a checklist in thread: 1) confirm no regressions in adapter logs for 30m; 2) monitor queue depth and HPA desired; 3) keep fallback route enabled until sustained <20 queue depth; 4) follow up on prometheus remote_write config.
Maya: ack. I'll watch for 30m then start rollback of emergency routing if stable.
Customer Success: customers confirmed perf improving, one asked for postmortem; CS notes customer-facing impact minimal after mitigations.
Samir: creating ticket INF-5136 to track permanent fixes: a) make adapter resilient to remote_write backpressure, b) add fallback metric source for HPA, c) alert on `custom.metrics.missing` sooner.
Devon (oncall): adding timeline notes to incident tracker. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maya: closing on-call shift; will keep monitoring and update if anything flares. Reacts: Devon :eyes:.
OpsBot: Incident status update: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident severity downgraded.
Samir: postmortem owner assigned: Samir. ETA for initial draft 48h.
Maya: will follow up with CS for customer comms and full RCA once postmortem draft is ready.
Devon (oncall): leaving final note: if metrics-adapter retries are common during remote_write saturation, consider local aggregation cache to keep HPA fed.
Maya: thanks, closing thread now.
